_meta.methodology: Median of N runs of `cargo test --test performance_regression_test --release test_performance_regression` (population=100, 1 warmup + 1 measured per run). Same harness CI's absolute-perf-gate (#2693) and performance.yml use. Computed via Python statistics.median (RULES.md constraint #0).
_meta.multi_zone_methodology: Median of 4 release-mode runs of `cargo test --test performance_regression_test --release test_multi_zone_performance_regression` (issue #2772: 10-zone ThermalModel, population=1000, analytical mode, 1 warmup + 1 measured per run). The multi-zone gate floor is `release_gates.yaml → benchmark.multi_zone.min_configs_per_sec: 10`; this baseline (50 cfg/sec) gives ~5x margin on dev-local. CI ubuntu-latest measurements may differ; the field is additive (no existing fields perturbed) and the test treats the absolute floor as the hard gate regardless of this baseline.
_meta.hybrid_methodology: HybridThermalModel (Issue #2922) absolute floors are captured as the same numeric value the release-gate YAML uses (`benchmark.hybrid.min_configs_per_sec: 80`, `benchmark.hybrid_multi_zone.min_configs_per_sec: 8`). The field is additive — the test never regresses against the absolute floor in any runner class; the per-runner baseline will be measured once `hybrid-perf-gate` runs enough times on ubuntu-latest to seed `enforcement: hard-gate`. Until then the absolute-floor assertion (which IS runner-independent) is the only enforcement. HybridThermalModel::from_spec(ASHRAE140Case::Case600.spec()) for single-zone, HybridThermalModel::new(10, HybridRouting::default()) for multi-zone — both use the production-recommended default routing (surrogate loads, physics everything else).
